transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I really appreciate it. 

I, um... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble keeping up with, you know, basic adult things lately? I'm sure it sounds silly, and I know a lot of people my age struggle a bit after college, right? But I just keep forgetting things. Like paying my bills, or... or following through on simple errands. I try really hard, I promise, but it just completely slips my mind. 

What finally made me come in, though, is that... well, this is really embarrassing to admit, but I've been missing appointments, and I keep forgetting to return interview emails. It's actually starting to cost me real opportunities, which makes me feel awful because I really do want to work. I just... I hope it's okay that I came in for this? Does that make sense?
Did you have similar problems with attention, organization, or forgetting things when you were a child?

Um, yeah... I guess I did. I mean, my teachers always made sure to write that I was a really bright kid, which was sweet of them, but... well, even back in elementary school, they would leave notes to my parents about how I was constantly losing my worksheets. 

I feel a little embarrassed admitting this, but my desk was always just so messy that I couldn't ever find my assignments when it was time to hand them in. And, um, I guess I had a bad habit of rushing through the directions? Like, I really wanted to do a good job, but I'd just go too fast. And I would accidentally talk out of turn a lot, too. I never meant to be disruptive, I promise, it just kind of... slipped out before I could catch myself. 

I always felt so bad about it because I really did want to be a good student. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm answering your question right.
